{{Short description|American theoretical physicist}}
'''Jonathan Anders Bagger''' (born August 7, 1955) is an American theoretical physicist, specializing in high energy physics and string theory and known for the [[Bagger–Lambert–Gustavsson action]].

Bagger received his bachelor's degree in 1977 from [[Dartmouth College]]. He spent the academic year 1977–1978 at the [[University of Cambridge]] as a Churchill Scholar. In 1978 he became a graduate student in physics at [[Princeton University]], where he received his PhD in 1983.<ref name=JHU>{{cite web|website=Henry A. Rowland Department of Physics & Astronomy, Johns Hopkins University|title=Jonathan A. Bagger|url=https://physics-astronomy.jhu.edu/directory/jonathan-a-bagger/}}</ref> His doctoral thesis ''Matter Couplings in Supergravity Theories'' was supervised by [[Edward Witten]].<ref>{{MathGenealogy|title=Jonathan A. Bagger|id=55213}}</ref> He was a postdoc from 1983 to 1986 at the [[Stanford Linear Accelerator Center]]. He was from 1986 to 1989 an associate professor at Harvard University. At [[Johns Hopkins University]] he became in 1989 a full professor, holding a professorial chair there until 2014. In 2014 he was appointed director of [[TRIUMF]], Canada's national laboratory for particle and nuclear physics.<ref name=JHU/><ref>{{cite web|author=Jepsen, Kathryn|title=Meet the next director of TRIUMF|date=28 April 2014|website=Symmetry Magazine, a joint Fermilab/SLAC publication|url=https://www.symmetrymagazine.org/article/april-2014/meet-the-next-director-of-TRIUMF}}</ref>

Bagger's research deals with high-energy physics, supersymmetry, and string theory. He was at Princeton's [[Institute for Advanced Study]] for the academic year 1985–1986<ref>{{cite web |author=Bagger, Jonathan A. |date=August 1986 |title=Twisted Strings and Orbifolds |website=Inspire HEP |s2cid=35573650 |url=https://inspirehep.net/files/009df285e9b59a7cdc4799d2cfcbdbda}}</ref> and in 1998.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jonathan Bagger|website=Institute for Advanced Study|url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/jonathan-bagger}}</ref> He was elected in 1997 a Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] and in 2008 a Fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science. He was an associate editor of ''[[Physical Review Letters]]'' from 1990 to 1993 and of ''[[Physical Review D]]'' from 1998 to 2007. He joined in 1997 the editorial board of the ''[[Journal of High Energy Physics]]'' and in 1998 the editorial board of ''[[Physics Reports]]''.<ref>{{cite web|title=Jonathan A. Bagger, CV|website=triumf.ca|url=https://www.triumf.ca/sites/default/files/Bagger_CV.pdf}}</ref>
